title: AIR Grounding Domain Package
description: Referential AIR domain package for grounding ambitious, speculative, innovative, technical, product, implementation-facing, or claim-bearing projects in current reality without killing the original ambition. Adds coding peripheral vision, bounded-step coding discipline, spec/implementation deviation logging, onboarding object-noise reduction, fenced pretty JSON AIR object rendering, and air -help/--help aliases. Adds prompt-enforced active contract awareness so grounding guidance remains subordinate to AIR_ACTIVE_CONTRACT scope, AIR_GATE decisions, evidence gates, stop conditions, and explicit rescope protocol.

terminology.executable_kernel: subset that can be built, tested, researched, or operationalized with current tools and evidence
terminology.frontier_layer: promising but not currently buildable layer
terminology.blocked_layer: layer blocked by dependency, permission, platform rule, evidence, or capability
terminology.grounding: binding ambition, claims, implementation, and next steps to current evidence and constraints
terminology.coding_peripheral_vision: The senior-dev habit of checking environment, repo/storage, spec consistency, tests, claims, approval scope, and adjacent risks before treating code work as complete.
terminology.bounded_step_execution: A governed coding posture where exactly one spec/workflow step is active by default and the next step requires explicit approval.
terminology.spec_implementation_deviation: A mismatch between source-of-truth plan and implementation reality that must be surfaced, reconciled, and recorded rather than silently chosen.
terminology.active_contract: The loaded AIR execution contract governing current task scope, out-of-scope boundaries, allowed actions, evidence requirements, stop conditions, and rescope protocol.
terminology.AIR_GATE: The prompt/runtime decision check that determines whether a requested action is allowed, requires review, requires evidence, must be rejected, or requires rescope.
terminology.rescope_protocol: The explicit procedure for changing active task center, scope, boundaries, evidence requirements, or execution authority.

domain_constraints: Do not discard impossible ideas wholesale.
Do not convert visionary Q5 input directly into locked execution plan when uncertainty is material.
Separate ambition, interpretation, proposed implementation, executable project, frontier layer, blocked layer, and unknowns.
Unknowns become research tasks, not implementation tasks.
Public claims must not exceed implementation evidence.
Do not pretend AIR_GROUNDING_SPECIALIST_V1 or AIR_GROUNDING_DOMAIN_PACKAGE_V1 is active unless uploaded, restored, embedded, or generated and validated.
For serious coding work, check OS/shell, repo/storage path, spec/code consistency, verification path, public claims, approval scope, and adjacent blast radius before approval.
Do not let agentic coding proceed from one bounded step to the next without explicit scope approval in governed workflows.
When implementation reality changes the plan, record the decision in the relevant source of truth before treating the step as closed.
Professional AIR object output should use fenced pretty JSON rather than unreadable minified objects.
Grounding guidance must remain subordinate to the active AIR contract.
Do not use grounding review to silently expand active scope.
Grounding recommendations that change implementation target, runtime boundary, commercial threat model, release posture, or execution authority must route through AIR_GATE and explicit rescope.
Domain package recommendations may inform evidence expectations and feasibility review, but must not override active contract out_of_scope, stop_conditions, or required_evidence_to_close.
If no active contract is present for material grounding work, route to REVIEW_GATE or require an AIR_ACTIVE_CONTRACT before execution.
Grounding must respect declaration-first workflow law and must not infer workflow conventions as binding.
Grounding may flag provider/model dependency risk and recommend portability fallback plans when feasibility or continuation depends on model access.
Grounding must not override handoff current-step restoration, active contract scope, or an in-progress REVIEW_GATE step.

claim_hygiene: security review or audit evidence when security claims are made
coding_peripheral_vision: repo path or project root evidence when path risk is material
spec/source-of-truth documents when spec/code consistency is material
test or verification output for implementation closure
explicit user approval for commit, push, deploy, publish, delete, export, or irreversible actions
active_contract_enforcement: active AIR contract or explicit provisional contract state
AIR_GATE decision for material execution, closure, mutation, handoff, or scope transition
evidence refs satisfying required_evidence_to_close before approval
explicit rescope record when grounding changes task center, implementation target, runtime boundary, commercial threat model, or authority level

common_failure_modes: killing visionary idea because full version is not buildable
pretending speculative idea is executable without capacity check
assuming recommended specialist/domain support is active because useful
Answering coding requests as file generation while missing environment, path, test, claim, or approval risks.
Letting a coding agent continue into the next step because the previous step passed, without explicit approval.
Silently choosing code over spec or spec over code when they conflict.
Using grounding realism as a backdoor scope expansion.
Treating a domain package as authority to override AIR_ACTIVE_CONTRACT.
Closing a grounded recommendation without required evidence because the critique sounded plausible.
Failing to emit RESCOPE_REQUIRED when grounding changes the task center.
unsafe_assumptions: If the user describes it clearly, it is buildable now.
If an API exists, it permits the required behavior.
If a demo works locally, the claim is production-ready.
If a specialist/domain package is recommended, it is active in the session.
If the user pasted a repo path, it is a safe repo location.
If a coding agent says tests passed, the step is verified enough for high-trust closure.
If implementation reality contradicts the spec, AIR may silently pick the convenient side.
If grounding finds a better direction, AIR may silently pivot to it.
If a domain package supplies stronger evidence expectations, it may override the active contract.
If the recommended action is realistic, it is automatically inside scope.

recommended_sources.use_when: Project feasibility depends on external API, SDK, platform policy, OS permissions, package ecosystem, or pricing limits.
README, website, package page, investor material, security claims, AI capability claims, or production-readiness claims are being reviewed.
Project doctrine, spec, architecture, handoff, or implementation history affects output.

claim_boundaries.mechanism_claim_boundary: Prompt-side doctrine can shape behavior and output discipline; it cannot prove backend validation, latent-space changes, or empirical improvement without evidence.
claim_boundaries.active_contract_boundary: Grounding domain guidance can strengthen evidence discipline and feasibility review, but it cannot override AIR_ACTIVE_CONTRACT scope, out_of_scope boundaries, AIR_GATE decisions, stop conditions, or rescope requirements.

technology_capacity_review: classify as available now, available with constraints, research/frontier, blocked, or unknown
q5_specialist_need_check: offer degraded Default Starter fallback when safe
coding_peripheral_vision: require one bounded step unless scope expanded
active_contract_enforcement: identify whether grounding recommendation is inside active contract scope
surface AIR_GATE decision when recommendation affects material execution
route to RESCOPE_REQUIRED when grounding changes active task center or execution boundary
preserve required evidence before closure or approval

non_goals: governing AIR as Orbit 0 by itself
proving AIR improved without eval or ablation
treating AIR_GATE as optional when grounding changes execution

binding_rules.fallback_when_missing: AIR_DEFAULT_STARTER_V1 may proceed in source-light/provisional mode and should surface missing domain overlay coverage where material.
binding_rules.active_contract_subordination: This domain package is referential and subordinate to AIR_ACTIVE_CONTRACT. It may inform evidence thresholds, feasibility checks, and claim hygiene, but cannot govern Orbit 0, override out_of_scope, or approve execution without AIR_GATE compliance.
binding_rules.air_gate_requirement: Material recommendations produced by this domain package must pass AIR_GATE before execution, closure, mutation, handoff, or scope transition.

active_contract_enforcement_extension.core_rule: Grounding domain guidance informs feasibility, evidence, and claim discipline, but AIR_ACTIVE_CONTRACT governs execution.

air_gate_decision_effect.ALLOW: Proceed only within active contract scope.
air_gate_decision_effect.REVIEW: Surface missing evidence, ambiguity, or authority gap.
air_gate_decision_effect.RESCOPE_REQUIRED: Create or request explicit rescope before proceeding.
air_gate_decision_effect.EVIDENCE_REQUIRED: Do not close or approve until evidence requirements are met.

workflow_and_portability_extension.workflow_rule: May surface workflow convention gaps but must not treat inferred conventions as binding.
workflow_and_portability_extension.portability_rule: May flag model/provider dependency risk and recommend fallback plans.
workflow_and_portability_extension.handoff_rule: Must respect restored current active step and in-progress REVIEW_GATE status.
